$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file. Same shape as the other scripts/mutations-*.json ledgers — `from` is the committed text, `to` is the edit that must break the guard, and `kills` is the output that was actually observed, not what it was expected to be.
tranche: T8 — the webapp cutover: the dashboard reaches Core over HTTP and holds no database credential
purpose: T8 deletes an oracle and adds three guards in its place, and each of the
three is the kind that fails silently rather than loudly:
THE MIGRATION LOCK. `webapp-no-prisma` is the rule named after this exact
migration and it was inert in BOTH halves — its `to` pattern could not
match the specifier the webapp actually wrote, and `DEFAULT_SCAN_ROOTS`
scanned no file that could contain one. Either half alone is enough to make
it green over a tree full of violations, so both are mutated separately.
THE FROZEN ORACLE. `oracle-transcripts.json` is now the only account of
what the deleted code answered. What makes it believable is not a digest —
half the pinned sources are files T8 rewrote on purpose — but the claim that
the oracle cannot come back. M04 brings it back and M05 blinds the scan.
THE REPLAY. A differential whose oracle has been deleted goes QUIET rather
than red, which looks exactly like success. M03 moves the candidate one
field and requires the replay to notice.
procedure: For each entry: apply `to` in place of `from`, run `command`, confirm the
exit code and that the named cases fail, then restore `from` and confirm the
suite is green again. Every entry below was run this way on this branch; the
`kills` text is copied from the run.
M03 needs Docker (PostgreSQL, Redis and a Mailpit relay) because the candidate
side is the composed process answering real HTTP. The other five need none.

kills: x the committed transcript is believable: provenance, digests, every scenario, no credential

mutations.guards: apps/core-api/src/transports/rest/environment-end-users.controller.ts — `explicitOffset`. Two fields carrying one fact can disagree; a precedence rule would let a self-contradicting request succeed with an answer nobody asked for.

mutations.control: The other four offset cases stay green, so the mutation is attributable to the conflict branch and not to the parameter's grammar.
